brief: Deutsche Bank's morning wrap reports a stagflation-driven selloff. With no end to the US-Iran conflict in sight and investors digesting reports that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen soon, Houthi capture of Mokha near Bab el-Mandeb raised Red Sea shipping and Saudi export fears, and Saudi output fell to its lowest since 1990. Brent rose 6.34% to $107.63/bbl, the six-month future to $88.85/bbl, and European natural gas 3.53% to a 2022 high, so investors are pricing a protracted period of high energy prices. That fed faster rate-hike speculation. The ECB hiked 25bp to 2.50% with hawkish forecasts, though Lagarde's Q&A took no view on direction, and markets moved to price three more ECB hikes against DB's call for one in December to 2.75%. A $5.19bn Treasury buyback, short of the $6bn maximum, added to the bond selloff: German 2yr +16.6bps, 10yr Treasury +12.2bps to 4.96%. August PPI at +0.4% with stronger PCE components lifted September Fed hike odds from 60% to 72%. The S&P 500 fell 0.58%, a fourth straight decline, and Asia followed. CPI is released today, DB forecasting +0.38% headline and +0.21% core.
